title: Constitutional Delay vs Familial Short Stature: Bone Age Delay and Testosterone Priming

steps.title: Clinical Triad of Constitutional Growth Delay

left.title: CDGP Profile
points: Delayed bone age > 2 years behind chronological age
Normal annual height velocity >= 4-5 cm/year
Delayed pubertal timing with family history of late blooming

right.title: Adult Outcome
points: Prolonged linear growth phase into late adolescence
Projected adult stature matches genetic potential
Excellent long-term auxological prognosis

steps.tx: CDGP is characterized by delayed bone age (> 2 years behind chronological age), normal height velocity (>= 4-5 cm/year), delayed pubertal onset, and positive family history of late puberty (late bloomer), reaching normal adult height. Recognizing the **Constitutional delay of growth and puberty (CDGP) triad** reassures families, as affected children track along the lower percentiles during early adolescence while their sustained prepubertal growth rate distinguishes benign physiology from organic failure.
steps.say: Constitutional delay features delayed bone age with normal growth velocity and late puberty, ultimately achieving target adult height.

steps.title: Familial Short Stature Diagnostic Criteria

left.title: Familial Short Stature
points: Bone age matches chronological age concordantly
Linear growth velocity remains normal for age
Pubertal onset and progression occur at normal age

right.title: Target Stature Alignment
points: Final height aligns with mid-parental target range
Both parents typically exhibit short adult height
Absence of dysmorphic or skeletal dysplasia signs

steps.tx: In familial short stature, bone age is concordant with chronological age (no delay), linear growth velocity is normal, pubertal timing is normal, and projected adult height falls exactly within mid-parental target range. Applying established **Familial short stature (FSS) criteria** confirms that children parallel the growth curves without deceleration or skeletal maturation lag. Comprehensive endocrine investigations remain unwarranted once mid-parental concordance and normal velocity are verified.
steps.say: Familial short stature presents with normal bone age, normal growth velocity, and final height matching the calculated parental target range.

steps.title: Standard Radiographic Bone Age Assessment

left.title: Radiographic Technique
points: Single frontal radiograph of left hand and wrist
Standard Greulich and Pyle skeletal atlas
Tanner-Whitehouse 3 (TW3) point scoring method

right.title: Clinical Interpretation
points: Delay > 2 standard deviations signifies skeletal lag
Correlates with biological maturity, not calendar age
Preserves long-term epiphyseal growth potential

steps.tx: Bone age is evaluated via single left hand-wrist radiograph using the Greulich and Pyle atlas or Tanner-Whitehouse (TW3) method; delay > 2 standard deviations signifies skeletal maturation delay. The **Bone age radiographic standard** assesses carpal bones, metacarpal epiphyses, and phalangeal growth plates undergoing stereotypic progressive ossification and fusion. Significant skeletal delay establishes biological immaturity and validates remaining growth potential.
steps.say: Skeletal maturity is quantified on a single left hand radiograph, where a delay beyond two standard deviations indicates significant maturation lag.

steps.title: Short-Course Testosterone Priming in Boys

nodes.label:
Adolescent Boy >= 14 yr
Severe psychosocial distress

Testosterone Enanthate
50-100 mg IM monthly for 3-6 mo

steps.tx: In adolescent boys >= 14 years with CDGP experiencing psychological distress, low-dose testosterone enanthate (50-100 mg IM monthly for 3-6 months) safely accelerates growth velocity and jump-starts hypothalamic GnRH without compromising final adult height. The **Short-course testosterone priming protocol** provides modest androgen exposure that triggers secondary sexual development and pubertal linear acceleration without advancing epiphyseal fusion prematurely.
steps.say: A brief low-dose testosterone course in adolescent boys over fourteen safely sparks pubertal progression without compromising final stature.

steps.title: Low-Dose Estrogen Priming in Adolescent Girls
steps.tx: In adolescent girls >= 13 years with CDGP, low-dose oral ethinyl estradiol (2-5 mcg daily) or transdermal estradiol for 3-6 months promotes secondary sexual characteristics and accelerates linear growth velocity. Implementing **Low-dose estrogen priming in girls** activates the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and stimulates hepatic IGF-1 synthesis. Limiting therapy duration preserves remaining epiphyseal cartilage.
steps.say: Low-dose estrogen therapy for three to six months in adolescent girls over thirteen jump-starts pubertal development and linear growth.

steps.title: Adult Stature Prediction via Bayley-Pinneau

left.title: Bayley-Pinneau Tables
points: Calculates percentage of mature height achieved
Utilizes Greulich-Pyle bone age and standing height
Stratifies by accelerated, average, or delayed maturity

right.title: Clinical Utility
points: Confirms normal projected final adult height
Provides essential reassurance to anxious families
Distinguishes benign delay from true growth failure

steps.tx: The Bayley-Pinneau tables predict final adult height based on current height and Greulich-Pyle bone age, distinguishing benign CDGP from true pathological growth hormone deficiency. Using **Bayley-Pinneau adult height prediction** shows that because the biological skeleton is younger than chronological age, substantial growth potential remains unspent. Demonstrating a normal projected adult height relieves psychosocial anxiety without growth hormone therapy.
steps.say: Bayley-Pinneau prediction tables utilize bone age to calculate final stature, verifying that constitutional delay reaches normal adult height.

steps.title: Auxological Red Flags for Pathological Stature

left.title: Auxological Red Flags
points: Height crossing percentiles downward
Subnormal annual velocity < 4 cm/year
Severe short stature below -3 SD

right.title: Physical and Systemic Signs
points: Disproportionate upper to lower segment ratio
Dysmorphic features or midline cranial defects
Unexplained gastrointestinal or systemic symptoms

steps.tx: Red flags signaling pathological growth failure include height crossing percentiles downward, subnormal height velocity (< 4 cm/year), disproportionate limb-to-trunk ratio (skeletal dysplasias), and dysmorphic features. Identifying **Pathological short stature red flags** prompts evaluation for systemic inflammatory conditions, celiac disease, occult craniopharyngioma, and Turner syndrome, which frequently manifest as isolated growth deceleration. Prompt auxological screening prevents irreversible stature loss.
steps.say: Decelerating growth velocity, crossing percentile channels downward, and skeletal disproportions highlight pathological short stature requiring investigation.

steps.title: Growth Hormone Indications for SGA Children

nodes.label:
Small for Gestational Age
Birth weight or length < -2 SD

Failure of Catch-Up
Height < -2 SD at 2-4 years

Endocrine Evaluation
Exclude syndromes and dysplasias

steps.tx: Children born Small for Gestational Age (SGA: birth weight or length < -2 SD) who fail to show spontaneous catch-up growth by 2-4 years of age qualify for rhGH somatropin therapy (0.067 mg/kg/day). Reviewing **SGA without catch-up growth indication** confirms that approximately 10% of infants born SGA fail to normalize stature spontaneously. Recombinant human somatropin growth hormone therapy restores childhood linear growth velocity, optimizes metabolic body composition, and normalizes adult height.
steps.say: Children born small for gestational age who lack spontaneous catch-up growth by age four qualify for recombinant growth hormone therapy.
